intro: South Carolina runs its elections county by county, through each county's board of voter registration and elections.

id_rule.text: Bring one current, valid photo ID: a South Carolina driver's license or DMV ID card, a South Carolina voter registration card with a photo, a federal military ID, or a U.S. passport. If you can't get a photo ID, you can sign a reasonable impediment affidavit, show your voter registration card, and vote a provisional ballot.

dates.label: Last day to register in person
dates.detail: Register at your county voter registration office by 5 pm. Some county boards hold weekend hours.

dates.detail: A mailed application must be postmarked by this date. The state's rule moves a postmark deadline that falls on a Sunday to the next day.

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Vote early at your county voter registration office or another early voting center, Monday through Saturday, 8:30 am to 6:00 pm. Centers are closed Sunday, Oct. 25. Bring a photo ID. Your county sets the locations.

dates.label: Absentee ballot application deadline
dates.detail: Your application must reach your county office by 5 pm, by U.S. mail or in person. Absentee voting is for voters who qualify, such as those 65 or older, people with a disability, or people who will be out of the county.

src.label: SC Election Commission - 2026 election calendar (Aug. 31, 2026 version)

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 7 pm. A voter in line at 7 pm can still vote. An absentee ballot must reach your county office by 7 pm.
